abstract: Background: Undernutrition increases tuberculosis (TB) risk, but whether severe undernutrition during latent TB infection (LTBI) produces blood transcriptional changes that resemble active disease or identify future TB remains unclear. Methods: We reanalyzed whole-blood RNA sequencing from adults with LTBI in GSE152218, comparing severe undernutrition (BMI <16 kg/m2; n=16) with adequate nutrition (BMI >=18.5 kg/m2; n=11). Genes and Reactome pathways were evaluated. A seven-module summary was compared with active TB among severely undernourished adults and tested prospectively in GSE79362 and GC6-74/GSE94438 after pathway-representation assessment. Results: No genes reached FDR <0.05 in the primary model; two did only in sensitivity analysis. In contrast, 241 Reactome pathways were significant and directionally concordant in both models (NES rho=0.954), including complement/Fc-receptor, B-cell, phospholipid/phagocytosis, neutrophil, vascular, autophagy, and cytokine-signaling pathways. Most changed opposite to the active-TB comparison (178/241; pathway rho=-0.390). The seven-module score was unrelated to baseline progression in GSE79362 (adjusted OR per SD=1.090; P=0.6922). In GC6, four modules met the prespecified representation criterion; their baseline score was inversely associated with progression (adjusted OR per SD=0.711; P=0.0218), but secondary and longitudinal analyses were non-confirmatory. Conclusions: Severe undernutrition during LTBI is associated with reproducible immune- and metabolism-related transcriptional remodeling that differs from active-TB biology and does not consistently identify future TB progression.
